thread:
sam: Heads-up — seeing a 2x p99 increase on the dedicated inference pool after the driver bump this morning (535.54). Affected models: redwood-v1 (short seq workload). tagging eng-runtime.
maria: Thanks — can you paste the profiler traces / sample requests?

sam: Pasting a short capture from the runtime profiler (filtered for short sequences):
```
11:30:02.123 model=redwood-v1 seq_len=32 batch=6 kernel=triton_flash_attention time_ms=18.4 workspace_est=1.2MB
11:30:02.124 model=redwood-v1 seq_len=32 batch=8 kernel=triton_flash_attention time_ms=19.1 workspace_est=1.4MB
11:30:02.125 model=redwood-v1 seq_len=128 batch=4 kernel=flash_attn time_ms=6.1 workspace_est=6.5MB
kv_cache_hit_ratio=0.08
```

rahul: This looks like a kernel-choice regression — selection now prefers the Triton variant for short seq/batch combos because workspace_est calculation changed with the new driver. Triton path adds extra memcpy/warp config that kills p99 on small batches. Also low kv_cache_hit makes short requests more sensitive to kernel overhead.

maria: Any host correlation? noisy neighbor?

perf-bot: automated-alert: p99 latency (short_seq) increased 2.1x on pool-dedicated-3 between 11:28–11:36 UTC; correlated hosts: host-37, host-42 (PCIe util spike).

jen: I repro'd locally with the same driver in a canary VM. When I force kernel preference to "flash_attn" in the selector, p99 returns to baseline. Quick toggles: `--kernel-pref flash_attn` on the process.

rahul: Proposed actions:
- Add temporary selector override on the affected pool to prefer flash_attn for seq<=48 until we ship a proper fix.
- Add kernel_choice + workspace_est telemetry at request-level (already discussed) so we can correlate quickly.
- Run a microbenchmark across seq/batch grid on 535.54 to produce a deterministic performance matrix and PR for the selector heuristics.

sam: +1 to override. Can infra patch the pool config? ops-bot, any rollback constraints?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolling selector override applied to pool-dedicated-3 at 11:45 UTC (applied preference: flash_attn for seq<=48). No downtime.

maria: Also add a short-term alert for kernel-choice shifts per-model so we get a page before a 2x p99.

rahul: I'll own the microbenchmark and a tentative selector tweak: prefer non-triton path for seq<=64 when batch<12 or kv_hit_ratio<0.2. Will post data in the eng-runtime thread.

sam: Great — after the override p99 for redwood-v1 short_seq is back to baseline on the pool. Leaving the thread open for the microbenchmark results and selector PR. :thumbsup:

jen: Filed reproducer + quick exploit script in the perf repo (link pasted in eng-runtime).

perf-bot: note: patch created — selector-heuristic/1985554321 in CI for benchmark run.

sam: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: telemetry, microbench, selector PR, consider driver-eng engagement if workspace_est calc requires driver-side clarification.
